findings.title: Meet bookings crash when no destination calendar is configured
findings.body: When `evt.destinationCalendar` is null or empty, destructuring leaves `mainHostDestinationCalendar` undefined, and this condition dereferences `.integration`. Creating an event with Google Meet and no destination calendar therefore throws before calendar or meeting events can be created; the previous optional-chain check handled this case.

findings.title: Non-Google calendar services receive the wrong destination for additional hosts
findings.body: `createAllCalendarEvents` invokes this function once per destination, passing that destination's external ID, but this call forwards only the credential ID to the calendar service. Lark, Office 365, and CalDAV creation still select `event.destinationCalendar[0]`, so calls for later hosts target the first host's calendar (or fail for lack of access) instead of the destination being processed. Collective bookings with multiple hosts using these integrations consequently fail to create events in each host's calendar.

findings.title: Google update cannot fall back to the configured destination calendar
findings.body: When `externalCalendarId` is absent, this lookup searches for a destination whose `externalId` equals that absent value, so it cannot select a configured destination calendar. `calendarId` is then undefined and Google event updates fail, even though the event contains the destination calendar. The analogous lookup in `deleteEvent` also falls through to `primary`, which can leave the event in its actual destination calendar.

findings.title: Rescheduling a multi-calendar booking deletes only one old calendar event
findings.body: This change collects and updates all calendar references, but the old-event cleanup below still uses `booking.references.find(...)` and deletes only the first calendar reference. When a booking has multiple host calendar events, rescheduling with `newBookingId` leaves the remaining old events on their calendars as stale duplicates.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation does not delete events for every calendar reference
findings.body: For recurring bookings, this loop iterates the organizer's credentials and then selects only the first calendar reference for each updated booking. It does not use the current reference being processed or match each booking reference to its credential. With multiple host calendar references, cancellation can repeatedly target the first calendar and leave the other hosts' recurring events behind.
